front?
It's a typo. We have corrected it, thanks.
Do we know how other system designers handle this?

Based on the information we have so far, the other projects do not require front panel LEDs, so we will proceed with the current implementation for now. If you have any further suggestions, we would be very grateful. Thank you.
Other systems have LEDs that are driven by error states though.  I'm not sure what the location of the LED has to do with anything here.

You mean we need to have the fault-monitor create an error log with a callout? Since this feature may require a longer development and validation time, we may need to first fix the current behavior in our existing firmware version. Would it be acceptable to treat the current implementation as a short-term solution, and consider "driven by error states" as a long-term goal? Thank you for your suggestion.
Why are you dropping the "RackFloorLeak1" and "RackFloorLeak2" from list of RACK_LEAKS?
According to the previous request from Meta, "RackFloorLeak1" and "RackFloorLeak2" should only log events and not trigger a power off.
Lets keep this var and use it as earlier.
ok, we kept this variable and used it as before, thanks.
Rename this to DetectorName
It has been renamed to DetectorName.
Lets rename this to LeakType
It has been renamed to LeakType.
Move all this into another function lets say EnableLeds() and call it based on LeakType.
These have been incorporated into EnableLeds() and are called based on the LeakType.
It was added by mistake and has been removedㄝ, thanks.
This should be processed earlier.
We processed these earlier.

Looks like you are adding lot of logic for Valve trains, why so? 

Are you using this script for some other purpose too?
As requested by the Meta and Thermal teams, the system must not power off before the valve train is closed. We have moved this part to a separate commit.
Please don't drop the cablemonitor as thats the feature we have recently enabled for Ventura.
Sorry, we accidentally dropped the CableMonitor and have now restored it.
leakdetector is already enabled for ventura through machine config, so you don't need to do it again.
Thank you for the reminder. We will no longer repeatedly enable the leakdetector.
I you have this check for RackLeaks, then why do you need the check at line#63? They seem redundant?
Yes, we've removed the redundant parts, thank you.
